title: Five classes of proofs of the Sons deity
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): ye Son has it communicated to Himself out from ye Father — for ye Father has it out from none. Distinction stands as in ye mode belonging toward subsisting by means belonging toward that same which each has divinity. according to ye Nicene synod homoousios with ye Father. Agreement stands as in one plus ye same nature plus essence — Philippians 2:6; From these things well established stands as gathered agreement plus distinction between Father plus Son. The fifth class stands as out from testimonies. VI. The fourth class stands as out from proper worship belonging toward God. V. The third class stands as out from divine works. IV. 1 Corinthians 2:8. Lord belonging toward glory — Revelation 19:16; — (3) He stands as called King belonging toward kings plus Lord belonging toward lords. John 1:18. (2) He stands as called Son belonging toward God properly plus univocally — Romans 8:32; Titus 2:13. Hebrews 1:8-9; Romans 9:5 — but also subjectively — 1 Timothy 3:16; For (1) He stands as called God not only attributively — John 1:1; The first class stands as out from ye names attributed to ye Son by means belonging toward Scripture. II. We demonstrate this chiefly by means belonging toward four distinct classes belonging toward arguments.
pass_b_english: We demonstrate this chiefly by four distinct classes of arguments. II. The first class is from the names attributed to the Son by Scripture. For (1) He is called God not only attributively — John 1:1; Romans 9:5 — but also subjectively — 1 Timothy 3:16; Hebrews 1:8-9; Titus 2:13. (2) He is called Son of God properly and univocally — Romans 8:32; John 1:18. (3) He is called King of kings and Lord of lords, Lord of glory — Revelation 19:16; 1 Corinthians 2:8.
IV. The third class is from divine works. V. The fourth class is from proper worship of God. VI. The fifth class is from testimonies.

From these things well established is gathered agreement and distinction between Father and Son. Agreement is in one and the same nature and essence — Philippians 2:6; according to the Nicene synod homoousios with the Father. Distinction is in the mode of subsisting by which each has divinity. For the Father has it from none, the Son has it communicated to Himself from the Father.
source_text: Hoc quatuor potissimum distinctis argumentorum classibus demonstramus. II. Prima classis est a nominibus Filio a Scriptura tributis. Nam 1. Deus dicitur non solum attributive — Joh. I.1; Rom. IX.5 — verum etiam subjective — I Tim. III.16; Heb. I.8-9; Tit. II.13. 2. Filius Dei dicitur proprie et univoce — Rom. VIII.32; Joh. I.18. 3. Dicitur rex regum et Dominus dominantium, Dominus gloriae — Apoc. XIX.16; I Cor. II.8. IV. Tertia classis est ab operibus divinis. V. Quarta classis est a cultu Dei proprio. VI. Quinta classis est a testimoniis. Ex his bene constitutis colligitur inter Patrem et Filium convenientia et distinctio. Convenientia est in una eademque natura et essentia — Phil. II.6; juxta Nicenam synodum homoousios Patri. Distinctio est in modo subsistendi, quo uterque divinitatem habet. Nam Pater eam habet a nullo, Filius a Patre sibi communicatam.
